blocks.text: Seth folded the blanket twice and slid it beneath the canvas practice bag.
“Your end first,” Jenny said.
He lifted just enough for her to straighten the fabric. Together they drew the bag across the mat, keeping it low and stopping at the strip of tape Billy had put on the floor.
Nothing scraped. Nothing tipped.
blocks.alt: Seth and Jenny practise moving a canvas bag together while Flaming Head watches in Claude’s training room.

blocks.text: Jenny looked at the bag, then at Seth.
“That would have helped with Frank.”
“If there’d been room to move him.”
“We’d have asked first.”
Seth nodded. He loosened his grip and sat back on his heels.

The training room in Claude’s building was quiet except for the radio in the adjoining office. Someone had left a pencil on the windowsill. Beside it, Flaming Head hovered over a clear patch of brick, watching them.
Jenny got up and crossed to the tape marks at the other end of the room. She walked the route once, looking at each turn before trying it at a run.
Seth moved the bag out of her way.
She set off. Her boots struck the mat in quick, separate beats. At the second mark she shortened her steps and stopped inside the square.
“Better,” Seth said.
“Slower.”
“You stopped where you meant to.”
Jenny looked down at her boots. Both were inside the tape.
“All right. Better.”
She went back to the first mark.
Flaming Head drifted away from the sill. His light followed her across the floor, faint in the afternoon sun.
When they finished, Seth carried the blanket to a shelf. Jenny opened the window a little farther and leaned her forearms on the brick ledge.
Below, a delivery van was backing toward a loading door. A man stood on the pavement, guiding the driver with slow movements of his hand.
Seth came to stand beside her.
“Things take longer,” Jenny said.
He watched the van stop short of the wall.
“They still get done.”
A familiar warmth touched them both.
Flaming Head had risen to the space between their shoulders. His orange face turned toward the street, then back to them.
“You’re finding ways.”
Jenny smiled a little.
“We could use a few more.”
“So could I.”
Seth looked at him properly. The little flame above his brow had settled low again.
“Does it hurt?”
“No.”
“Are you getting any stronger?”
Flaming Head stayed level with the sill.
“Not here.”
Jenny straightened.
“What do you mean?”
“I need more power.”
blocks.alt: Flaming Head speaks with Seth and Jenny beside an open window overlooking Cleveland.

blocks.text: Seth waited. Beyond the window, the man guiding the van lowered his hand.
“There’s somewhere I can look for it.”
“Where?” Jenny asked.
“The Sun.”
For a moment she only looked at him. Then she turned toward the bright afternoon beyond the roofs.
“You can go all that way?”
“I can reach it.”
“If I can find more energy there, it may help you too.”
Seth moved the curtain clear of the little flame.
“You should have told us you were thinking about this.”
“I’m telling you now.”
There was no sharpness in the answer. Flaming Head looked from Seth to Jenny, waiting while they took it in.
Billy came to the doorway carrying the street map. Fist followed at his shoulder.
“Anything changed?” Billy asked.
Jenny glanced at Seth.
“He’s going to the Sun,” Seth said. “To find more power.”
Billy stopped beside the table.
“The actual Sun?”
Seth nodded.
Fist drifted closer to Flaming Head, then turned to Jenny for an explanation.
“That’s farther than the lake.”
“He says he can reach it,” she told him.
Billy laid the map down carefully. He looked at the little flame, but waited for Seth to speak again.
“He thinks it could help us too.”
“That would be useful,” Fist said. “I’ve been doing all the impressive hovering lately.”
blocks.alt: Billy, Fist-O-Mite, Seth and Jenny gather around the map table as Flaming Head shares his plan.

blocks.text: Jenny laughed before she could stop herself.
“You have.”
Fist gave a small, pleased turn.
Billy pulled a chair away from the table so everyone had room.
“Is there anything we can do here?”
Flaming Head turned toward him.
“Keep helping people.”
Seth repeated it aloud.
Billy nodded. “We can manage that.”
Jenny looked at the marks on the training-room floor.
“We’ll keep practising.”
Flaming Head’s eyes followed hers.
“Ask for help when you need it.”
She gave him a look.
“We did get the jack.”
“I know.”
She smiled then, properly.
Seth felt the small warmth of his friend’s attention turn toward him.
“You don’t have to lift everything by yourself.”
He looked down at his hands.
“I’m learning.”
Billy went to the operations desk and checked that the radio was turned up. Fist followed him to look at the list of calls beside it.
Jenny stayed at the window with Seth and Flaming Head.
“Do you want us to tell anyone else?” she asked.
“Tell them I’ve gone to find more power.”
“That part’s easy,” Seth said. “Explaining where you went might take longer.”
Jenny reached for the pencil on the sill, then stopped.
“This isn’t a newspaper story.”
“Not yet,” Seth said.
She set the pencil beside the curtain and left it there.
Outside, the van’s rear doors opened. The two men began unloading it, passing each box between them.
Flaming Head rose a few inches.
Seth opened the window all the way.
“Mind the frame,” Jenny said.
The little face turned toward her. One brow lifted.
“I can see it.”
“I know.”
He passed over the sill, then paused beyond the glass while Seth held the curtain back.
“Look after each other.”
“We will,” Jenny said.
Seth repeated the words for Billy and Fist, who had come back to the doorway.
Billy raised one hand.
“Safe journey.”
Fist floated up beside the open window.
“Find something good.”
Seth looked at the small orange face.
“We’ll be here.”
Flaming Head’s eyes moved across the four friends. Then he turned toward the open sky.
At first they could follow him easily.
blocks.alt: The four friends watch Flaming Head rise above the rooftops through the facility’s open window.

blocks.text: He rose above the neighboring roof, cleared its chimney and kept going. The late sun caught the upper windows across the street. For a moment his little light passed against the dark brick and showed bright again.
Jenny leaned closer to the opening.
“There.”
Seth found him above the roofline.
Then a pale cloud slipped behind the flame, and the orange point became difficult to pick out.
Fist lifted himself higher to see past the window frame.
“Still going?”
Seth watched until he could no longer be certain which bright speck he was following.
“Yes.”
Billy stood beside them for another moment. Then a voice broke through the radio behind him.
He turned to listen.
Jenny drew back from the sill. On the training-room floor, the tape marks waited where she had left them.
“We should move that square,” she said. “The second turn’s too close to the wall.”
Seth looked once more at the sky, then followed her.
Above the blue curve of the world, the sky deepened until the scattered stars stood clear.
blocks.alt: Flaming Head travels steadfastly through black space toward the Sun, with blue Earth receding behind him.

blocks.text: Flaming Head kept his course.
Clouds covered part of the Earth behind him. The lake and its rows of lights had become too small to see. Ahead lay the Sun, bright across the darkness.
He turned his face toward it. His eyes held steady beneath the small crown of flame.
Then he went on.
